record.what_it_does: Cloud communications APIs for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, video and verification.
record.auth_notes: Requests use HTTP Basic auth. The recommended form sends an API Key SID as the username and the Key Secret as the password. The alternative sends the Account SID and Auth Token, which some endpoints require. OAuth 2.0 client credentials has been GA for the Communications APIs since Apr 6, 2026: a token from POST oauth.twilio.com/v2/token is passed as a Bearer token and expires after 1 hour. Organization-level OAuth apps also support the Authorization Code grant, which is intended for apps acting on behalf of a user. The docs don't say whether third-party apps can use it on other customers' accounts. In practice a multi-user toolkit would collect each user's Account SID plus an API key and secret.
record.access_notes: The free trial needs no credit card. According to the trial page it gives product-specific free units, such as 100 SMS and 75 voice minutes, lasts 30 days, and only allows sending to up to 5 verified numbers. Production use needs an upgrade to a paid, pay-as-you-go account. A2P 10DLC registration also requires a paid account. There is no permanent free tier.
record.api_breadth_notes: Each product has its own REST API: Messaging, Voice, Lookup, Verify, Conversations, Studio, Video, Sync, TaskRouter, IAM and others. Twilio's own MCP announcement says it covers more than 1,800 APIs.
record.mcp_notes: Twilio hosts an official MCP server at https://mcp.twilio.com/docs, in Public Beta since May 2026. It only searches and retrieves documentation through two tools, twilio__search and twilio__retrieve. It takes no credentials and cannot call any APIs. Twilio lists OAuth-authenticated MCP tools that execute API calls as a future item ("What's next"). For actual API calls, Twilio publishes the local package @twilio-alpha/mcp (github.com/twilio-labs/mcp), labeled "Twilio Alpha". It runs through npx and authenticates with an Account SID plus an API key and secret, and its README calls it one of "our official" servers.
record.blocker_notes: The API is public and documented, and credentials are self-serve. The caveats: trial accounts expire after 30 days and can only send to verified numbers. Real traffic needs a paid pay-as-you-go account plus regulatory work such as A2P 10DLC registration, which itself requires a paid account. Test credentials work on only 4 endpoints: buying phone numbers, sending messages, placing calls and Lookup; any other endpoint returns 403. Multi-user auth means collecting per-account API keys, or OAuth client credentials, which the user also has to set up.
